audit.why: Ziggs owns the poke phase 1-3, Vladimir tilts it from 4-5 on and hard-outscales; 54% WR over 2152 real games (note: this matchup was once wrongly skipped on packet.games=0 — MC_REAL_GAMES wins).

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer chart had Ziggs on row 3 and blanket 'Skill' on rows 4-6 while content win[] and the packet levelChart give Vladimir rows 3-6. Content whys also shipped with visible 'win[N]=...' debug prefixes.
audit.why: Content and packet charts agree on Z,Z,Z,V,V,V,V.
audit.corrected: Full sides flipped with why rewrites; prefixes stripped.

audit.whatIsWrong: Content repeatedly claims Ziggs's R displaces ('W's through... R displacement', 'W dodges Ziggs's displacement'). Mega Inferno Bomb is a damage zone with no knockback — only Satchel Charge (W) displaces. Also the missing-interactions 'resistances-invalidated / percentHealth' flag on W contradicts Riot's own W text (no percent-health language against champions; the turret hexplode likely tripped the parser) — per the calibration rule the description wins, so no percent-health claim was written. Short Fuse auto-reset tell folded in.
audit.why: enemyKit R text: damage zone only; W text is the only knockback.
audit.corrected: R described as burst to Pool, not displacement; Satchel is the sole knockback.

audit.why: Kit: W 20-12s, Q 6-4s at 50+ mana, R 120s, Vlad W 28s.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback escape — he is catchable only while it is down. Count it out loud if you must. - Your W Sanguine Pool has one job: the moment it all goes wrong. - The R has one too: the moment it all goes right.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1, 12s max — his only escape; he is catchable exactly that often, so count it. - Bouncing Bomb runs 6-4s at 50+ mana — poke gaps are short but the mana drain is real. - Your 28s Pool answers Mega Inferno Bomb, not chip.

edits.before: Q the last-hit, E-charge as he steps to answer, release and walk — the trade costs him HP and pays yours.
edits.after: Mega Inferno Bomb is the only spell here worth a Pool — trading your 28s cooldown for his 120s ult wins every time.

edits.before: Pooling his poke and then eating the real engage at half HP with nothing — the pool is a combo-breaker, not a flinch reflex.
edits.after: A held E charge at half HP in his 850-range Q arc is the chunk he farms — his Short Fuse auto follows every bomb.

edits.before: Vlad hard-outscales this matchup. With full build his HP pool shrugs off poke, W dodges Ziggs's displacement and burst, and he dives the immobile mage on demand. In teamfights Hemoplague amplifies his AoE and he simply outlasts Ziggs, who has no escape once Vlad reaches him.
edits.after: Vlad hard-outscales this matchup. With full build his HP pool shrugs off poke, W dodges the Satchel knockback and R burst, and he dives the immobile mage on demand. In teamfights Hemoplague amplifies his AoE and he simply outlasts Ziggs, who has no escape once Vlad reaches him.
